messages:
maria: Heads-up — the onboarding sample app is producing steady 429s when a new org ramps to ~12 concurrent requests. repro steps below, and the behavior looks like a client-side throttling/backpressure mismatch + token refresh interaction.

maria: repro steps:
1) run sample app (master) with default client config
2) spawn 12 parallel workers hitting /generate + pagination of embeddings for each result
3) after ~30s we start seeing 429 spikes and a big burst of success responses after ~3-4s stalls

maria: logs (trimmed):
```
2025-11-02T15:12:03Z INFO worker-3 request start id=abc123
2025-11-02T15:12:03Z WARN client token refresh started
2025-11-02T15:12:06Z INFO client token refresh finished
2025-11-02T15:12:06Z INFO worker-3 request sent id=abc123 status=429
2025-11-02T15:12:07Z INFO client queued 11 requests during refresh
2025-11-02T15:12:07Z INFO client drained queue -> burst send (many 429s)
```

maria: sample app: https://github.com/redwood/sample-onboard/tree/main/throttle-demo (using default SDK config)

rate-limiter-bot: :warning: Detected high 429 rate for token org-999 (rate limit window: 60s)

tj: Thanks — can you paste the SDK config used by the sample? is it JS or Python?

maria: JS (node 20), default @redwood/sdk client, no custom backoff configured. concurrency: we spawn worker threads in the app not via SDK.

kevin: FWIW we had a parity note: JS SDK uses a token-bucket style limiter with burst=8 by default; Python had a simple queue that serializes. That could explain the "burst after refresh" pattern. if requests are queued during refresh then all get released at once and blow past server-side quota.

sophia: Also: current JS SDK does a synchronous token refresh under mutex, which blocks the request path. That means the client queues up outbound requests until refresh completes. Combined with a token-bucket burst allowance on the transport, you get a big simultaneous send right after refresh.

kevin: Repro hypothesis: 1) token expires -> sync refresh blocks the pool -> app threads accumulate requests -> refresh returns and token-bucket allows bursts -> server applies global quota -> many 429s.

maria: yep that's what the logs show. any quick mitigation we can push to sample app/docs before we ship the onboarding?

tj: short-term patch: in sample app set SDK option "maxConcurrency: 6" + enable exponential backoff with Full Jitter (base=200ms, cap=2s). That should smooth the post-refresh spike. Also avoid prefetching paginated pages concurrently — fetch pages sequentially or stream them.

devex-intern: I can open a PR to change the sample app defaults and add a note in quickstart about token refresh/backpressure. should I also add an example of client-side leaky-bucket?

kevin: Yes please. Also file an SDK issue to change JS SDK behavior: either make token refresh non-blocking (background refresh with optimistic requests) or fail fast with 401 and let the retry/backoff handle it. Background refresh is trickier but better UX.

sophia: For short term we should also update docs: "If you have bursty concurrent workloads (>=8 concurrent streams), set client maxConcurrency and enable jittered backoff. Avoid starting many pagination workers in parallel — stream pages or limit parallel page fetches to 2."

maria: question: pagination + embeddings + batching — any known guidance? we were doing: for each page of results spawn a request to embeddings endpoint. that multiplied tokens and concurrency.

kevin: Don't batch page-to-embeds concurrently unless your embeddings provider supports concurrent throughput. Instead accumulate N items per page and submit a single batch embedding request. Or serialize page processing: process page i, send embedding batch, then fetch page i+1. That keeps peak concurrency low.

tj: Action items:
- devex-intern: PR to change sample default: maxConcurrency=6, add backoff snippet, and add paragraph on pagination/embeddings (due EOD local)
- kevin: open SDK issue for JS token-refresh parity with Python (background refresh proposal + notes)
- sophia: update quickstart docs with explicit "concurrency + pagination" section and recommended defaults

maria: I'll test the sample with the patched defaults and report numbers (latency/429 rate) here. thanks all :thumbsup:

rate-limiter-bot: :white_check_mark: Noted: reduced defaults suggested for onboarding sample (maxConcurrency=6).
